<h1 align="center">NanoC</h1>

<p align="center"><b>Less syntax, full control.</b> A compact, self-hosted language that generates plain C11 or C++17.<br>Indented blocks, programmable macros, compile-time source transformations, compact C preprocessing.</p>

<p align="center"><a href="https://mkalmousli.github.io/NanoC/">Website</a> · <a href="docs/language.md">Language card</a> · <a href="docs/architecture.md">Architecture</a> · <a href="src/editors.tool.nc">Editors</a></p>

## Quick start

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mkalmousli/NanoC && cd NanoC && cc -std=c11 -O2 build.c -o builder && ./builder install
```

Needs git and a C11 compiler (`cc`, `gcc` or `clang`). Installs `nanoc` to `~/.local/bin` and sets up the editors it detects. Add `--no-editors` to skip editors, or `--prefix DIR` to change the location.

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install | `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mkalmousli/NanoC && cd NanoC && cc -std=c11 -O2 build.c -o builder && ./builder install` |
| Update | `nanoc update` |
| Uninstall | `nanoc uninstall` (asks first; `--yes` skips) |
| Custom location | `./builder install --prefix DIR` |
| Editor syntax | `nanoc editor install vim` (see [Editors](#editors)) |

Installs only the files it created; it refuses to overwrite unrelated files.

## The language

```c
+ <stdio.h>
f main()
  printf("Hello from NanoC! %d %g\n", 6 * 7, 1.5)

```

- **Layout:** indentation defines blocks; `f name(args)` with an optional result type (void by default, int for main); explicit `<` returns; `if/elif/else`, `while` and `for` controls.
- **Macros:** `@m` token templates with `$` captures, repetition and `$fresh(name)`.
- **Compile time:** `@ct` programs generate code during expansion (`emit`, `quote`, loops).
- **Interop:** C headers and C++17 APIs work unchanged (`--lang c++`).
- **Agent-friendly:** `nanoc --describe syntax|builtins`, `nanoc file.nc --check --diagnostics json`.

Output is ordinary C with no NanoC runtime. `@bt` and NanoC assembly were removed; host commands belong in external build tools and compiler extensions in `@c`. Full reference: [language card](docs/language.md) or `nanoc --describe syntax`.

## Runs wherever C runs

- **Host:** Linux, macOS, BSD and Windows: the compiler is plain portable C11 (cross-compiled with MinGW in CI); building it from source uses a POSIX shell such as sh, MSYS2 or Git Bash.
- **Output:** C89/C99/C11/C17 syntax modes, or secondary C++17 with `--lang c++`. User C must satisfy the chosen standard.

## Editors

Generated from one token table in [src/editors.tool.nc](src/editors.tool.nc) and installed for detected editors.

```sh
nanoc editor list
nanoc editor install vim       # or --all, or no args for detected editors
nanoc editor remove vim
```

| Editor | Command | Installs to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VS Code, VSCodium, Cursor | `nanoc editor install vscode` | extension folder under `~/.vscode`, `~/.vscode-oss`, `~/.cursor` |
| Vim | `nanoc editor install vim` | `~/.vim/syntax`, `~/.vim/ftdetect` |
| Neovim | `nanoc editor install neovim` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/nvim` |
| Emacs | `nanoc editor install emacs` | `~/.emacs.d/lisp` (prints the `require` line) |
| micro | `nanoc editor install micro` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/micro/syntax` |
| GNU nano | `nanoc editor install nano` | `~/.nano/nanoc.nanorc` (prints the `include` line) |
| Sublime Text 4 | `nanoc editor install sublime` | `Packages/User` |

## Build from source

```sh
cc -std=c11 -O2 build.c -o builder
./builder bootstrap   # C seed -> NanoC -> NanoC, byte-identical
./builder test        # GCC + Clang, real C, sanitizers
CC=clang ./builder test --sanitize
./builder docs        # regenerate README and docs from src/docs
```

## Project

- Compiler, tools, docs and editors are NanoC under `src/`; compiler modules are at most 200 lines.
- `build.c` is the only hand-written C; `bootstrap/` keeps a generated C seed.
- Tests are offline. Corpus provenance: [tests/corpus](tests/corpus/README.md).
